mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) as a continuous variable predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce the discount rate for equity valuation and increase the attractiveness of equities relative to bonds.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below 1.5% (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL value exceeding 250.0 indicates elevated inflation, which triggers a negative market reaction due to reduced real returns and potential central bank tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL > 250.0 (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A low real interest rate (FEDFUNDS - CPIAUCSL) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as it indicates accommodative monetary policy that supports equity valuations. The signal is derived from the interaction of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL.
failure_condition: The interaction signal (FEDFUNDS - CPIAUCSL) does not yield positive returns in more than 60% of instances when the real rate is below 1.0% (or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A regime characterized by weak housing starts (HOUST < 1300) and declining residential sales (RSAFS < 500000) predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to heightened recession risks and reduced consumer confidence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative when HOUST < 1300 and RSAFS < 500000 (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A UNRATE exceeding 4.5% indicates a weakening labor market, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to heightened recession fears and reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 4.5% (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of PAYEMS below 148000 and UNRATE above 4.0% indicates a deteriorating labor market, predicting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and business investment.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS < 148000 and UNRATE > 4.0% (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A higher INDPRO (as a continuous variable) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as it indicates strong industrial activity and economic growth, which supports equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO > 105 (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A HOUST value below 1300 indicates a weakening housing market, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced consumer confidence and economic slowdown concerns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative when HOUST < 1300 (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.
